metrics.label: Washed kg

metrics.label: Allocation use rate
metrics.formula: SUM(active_assets_scanned) / SUM(allocated_pieces), latest reporting month | Live arithmetic (display rounded to 6 decimals; result in ratio): 26,513 scanned / 31,743 allocated = 0.835239; stock month 2025-12

metrics.label: Idle pieces
metrics.formula: SUM(allocated_pieces - active_assets_scanned), latest reporting month | Live arithmetic (display rounded to 6 decimals; result in pieces): 31,743 allocated - 26,513 scanned = 5,230; stock month 2025-12

metrics.label: Illustrative idle stock value
metrics.formula: SUM((allocated_pieces - active_assets_scanned) * synthetic_purchase_cost_eur), latest month; illustrative stock value | Live arithmetic (display rounded to 6 decimals; result in EUR): P1001: (10,173 - 8,293) * 54 EUR/piece + P1002: (10,561 - 8,982) * 39 EUR/piece + P1004: (11,009 - 9,238) * 34 EUR/piece; illustrative stock value, not savings = 223,315; stock month 2025-12

metrics.label: Wash frequency
metrics.formula: SUM(washed_pieces) / SUM(active_assets_scanned), weighted across reporting months | Live arithmetic (display rounded to 6 decimals; result in washes/active asset/month): 749,306 washed pieces / 319,260 active-asset observations across months = 2.347009

metrics.label: Service requests
metrics.formula: SUM(service_requests) | Live arithmetic (display rounded to 6 decimals; result in requests): SUM(service_requests) over 864 selected rows = 515

metrics.label: On time rate
metrics.formula: COUNT(ON_TIME) / COUNT(cycles); period selected by pickup_timestamp | Live arithmetic (display rounded to 6 decimals; result in ratio): 11181 on-time cycles / 11371 cycles (pickup month) = 0.983291

metrics.label: Median cycle hours
metrics.formula: MEDIAN(cycle_hours); period selected by pickup_timestamp | Live arithmetic (display rounded to 6 decimals; result in hours): 11371 sorted cycle-hour observations; middle value(s): 82 = 82

metrics.label: Repairs total
metrics.formula: SUM(repair_count) | Live arithmetic (display rounded to 6 decimals; result in repairs): SUM(repair_count) over 2500 selected rows = 15,233

metrics.label: Repair rate per 1000
metrics.formula: SUM(repair_count) / SUM(washed_pieces) * 1000 | Live arithmetic (display rounded to 6 decimals; result in repairs/1000 washed pieces): 15,233 repairs / 749,306 washed pieces * 1,000 = 20.329478

metrics.label: Replacements postponed
metrics.formula: SUM(repair_count) * repair_factor | Live arithmetic (display rounded to 6 decimals; result in events): 15,233 repairs * 1 repair factor = 15,233; scenario=base; baseline=B_LOCAL

metrics.label: Avoided product co2e kg
metrics.formula: SUM(repair_count * synthetic_product_footprint_kgco2e) * repair_factor | Live arithmetic (display rounded to 6 decimals; result in kgCO2e): (P1001: 5,816 repairs * 18.5 kgCO2e/product + P1002: 5,168 repairs * 13.2 kgCO2e/product + P1004: 4,249 repairs * 11.4 kgCO2e/product) * 1 repair factor = 224,252.2; scenario=base; baseline=B_LOCAL

metrics.label: Customer water l
metrics.formula: SUM(customer_washed_kg * fresh_water_l / laundry washed_kg) | Live arithmetic (display rounded to 6 decimals; result in L): 502,074.7 kg * 6.698384 effective weighted amount/kg = 3,363,089.359656; effective intensity is derived from the sum of row allocations, not a uniform source factor

metrics.label: Customer energy kwh
metrics.formula: SUM(customer_washed_kg * process_energy_kwh / laundry washed_kg) | Live arithmetic (display rounded to 6 decimals; result in kWh): 502,074.7 kg * 0.708136 effective weighted amount/kg = 355,537.127713; effective intensity is derived from the sum of row allocations, not a uniform source factor

metrics.label: Customer co2e kg
metrics.formula: SUM(customer_washed_kg * (process_emissions_kgco2e + delivery_emissions_kgco2e) / laundry washed_kg) | Live arithmetic (display rounded to 6 decimals; result in kgCO2e): 50,000.513955 allocated process kgCO2e + 23,784.72994 allocated delivery kgCO2e = 73,785.243895

metrics.label: Textile waste kg
metrics.formula: SUM(customer_washed_kg * waste_kg_per_washed_kg) | Live arithmetic (display rounded to 6 decimals; result in kg): 502,074.7 kg * 0.033459 effective weighted amount/kg = 16,798.673198; effective intensity is derived from the sum of row allocations, not a uniform source factor

metrics.label: Circular waste share
metrics.formula: SUM(allocated recycling_kg + allocated reuse_kg) / SUM(allocated textile_waste_kg) | Live arithmetic (display rounded to 6 decimals; result in ratio): (12,279.013171 recycling kg + 818.922762 reuse kg) / 16,798.673198 attributed waste kg = 0.779701

metrics.label: Water saving l
metrics.formula: SUM(customer_washed_kg) * B.water_l_per_kg * baseline_factor - customer_water_l | Live arithmetic (display rounded to 6 decimals; result in L): 502,074.7 kg * 9.5 baseline/kg * 1 baseline multiplier - 3,363,089.359656 customer footprint = 1,406,620.290344; scenario=base; baseline=B_LOCAL

metrics.label: Energy saving kwh
metrics.formula: SUM(customer_washed_kg) * B.energy_kwh_per_kg * baseline_factor - customer_energy_kwh | Live arithmetic (display rounded to 6 decimals; result in kWh): 502,074.7 kg * 1.05 baseline/kg * 1 baseline multiplier - 355,537.127713 customer footprint = 171,641.307287; scenario=base; baseline=B_LOCAL

metrics.label: Co2e saving kg
metrics.formula: SUM(customer_washed_kg) * (B.process_kgco2e_per_kg + B.delivery_kgco2e_per_kg) * baseline_factor - customer_co2e_kg | Live arithmetic (display rounded to 6 decimals; result in kgCO2e): 502,074.7 kg * (0.62 process + 0.035 delivery) baseline/kg * 1 baseline multiplier - 73,785.243895 customer footprint = 255,073.684605; scenario=base; baseline=B_LOCAL

industry_rules: Food & Beverage #1: Hygiene and compliance — Show service continuity, food-industry garment control and hygiene-related performance.
Food & Beverage #2: Water efficiency — Prioritize water use/savings and washed-kg efficiency.
Food & Beverage #3: Service reliability — Highlight turnaround, service-request-free days and delivery performance.

observations.title: Water value against the selected baseline
observations.observation: Water savings are allocated estimates against the selected baseline, with low/base/high uncertainty. Evidence: water_saving_l: Low 452,678.36 / Base 1,406,620.29 / High 2,360,562.22 L. Highest washed_kg: S008: 38,379.2 kg; S001: 36,207.3 kg; S007: 34,072.3 kg. Why it matters: Food & Beverage teams need reliable garment availability for hygiene workflows.
observations.recommended_action: Proposed Q1 2026 planning scenario (KAM must confirm or reschedule): Validate water intensity and the selected baseline at 3 highest-volume sites covering 108,658.8 kg. Set an improvement target only after source validation. Potential benefit: better water-efficiency decisions; the existing baseline saving is not additional future saving.
observations.steering_question: Which site/source owner will confirm this scope, the proposed benefit and a comparable follow-up measure? Which baseline best represents the customer alternative?

observations.title: Review service continuity at late-cycle sites
observations.observation: These sites fall below the customer on-time benchmark. Evidence: on_time_rate: S008: 97.22%; S014: 97.72%; S022: 97.82%. Benchmark: customer_on_time_rate: 98.33%. Why it matters: Food & Beverage teams need reliable garment availability for hygiene workflows.
observations.recommended_action: Proposed Q1 2026 planning scenario (KAM must confirm or reschedule): Review pickup schedules at 15 flagged sites. Maximum benchmark gap: 1.11 percentage points. Propose closing the gap to the customer benchmark, subject to feasibility; late-cycle counts are unavailable. Potential benefit: more dependable garment availability; improvement is not guaranteed.
observations.steering_question: Which site/source owner will confirm this scope, the proposed benefit and a comparable follow-up measure? Which schedule changes could improve service continuity?

observations.title: Investigate high service-request intensity
observations.observation: Service requests per estimated minimum wearer exceed the site-median threshold. The denominator is an estimate. Evidence: service_requests per 1,000 wearers: S022: 172.13; S003: 138.61; S004: 113.77. Benchmark: customer_site_median: 56.23. Why it matters: Food & Beverage teams need reliable garment availability for hygiene workflows.
observations.recommended_action: Proposed Q1 2026 planning scenario (KAM must confirm or reschedule): Classify 99 reported requests at 5 flagged sites. Maximum gap above site median: 115.9 requests per 1,000 estimated wearers. Validate wearer denominators before setting reduction targets. Potential benefit: address recurring service issues; counts alone cannot establish causes or response times.
observations.steering_question: Which site/source owner will confirm this scope, the proposed benefit and a comparable follow-up measure? Which request categories should the teams address first?

observations.title: Review allocation at the lowest-use sites
observations.observation: Lowest-use sites warrant an allocation review; unscanned stock is not proof of waste. Evidence: allocation_use_rate: S010: 75.57%; S001: 76.21%; S024: 78.55%. Why it matters: Food & Beverage teams need reliable garment availability for hygiene workflows.
observations.recommended_action: Proposed Q1 2026 planning scenario (KAM must confirm or reschedule): Review 5 flagged sites: 1,434 reported idle pieces. Confirm shift buffers before any rebalance; this is investigation scope, not removable stock. Potential benefit: better stock utilization while maintaining availability; no cost saving is established.
observations.steering_question: Which site/source owner will confirm this scope, the proposed benefit and a comparable follow-up measure? Where can we pilot an allocation review while maintaining garment availability?

observations.title: Resolve evidence gaps before external reporting
observations.observation: Data-quality warnings and missing production sources limit the conclusions. Sources to resolve: Customer hierarchy is synthetic; Unique wearer count. Additional gaps: 6; see the data-readiness registry. Checks: DQ1, DQ4, PACK_DATA_STATUS, DQ5_WEARER_MULTI_PRODUCT_SUM. Why it matters: Food & Beverage teams need reliable garment availability for hygiene workflows.
observations.recommended_action: Proposed Q1 2026 planning scenario (KAM must confirm or reschedule): Triage 8 data gaps and 22 finding records across 4 distinct checks. Assign source owners and agree evidence acceptance criteria before external claims. Potential benefit: more defensible customer discussions; finding records can repeat the same issue across months.
observations.steering_question: Which site/source owner will confirm this scope, the proposed benefit and a comparable follow-up measure? Which missing production source should we connect first?
